name: pont Notre-Dame
text: The Pont Notre-Dame (French pronunciation: [pɔ̃ nɔtʁə dam]) is a bridge that crosses the Seine in Paris, France linking the quai de Gesvres on the Rive Droite with the quai de la Corse on the Île de la Cité. The bridge is noted for being the "most ancient" in Paris, in the sense that, while the oldest bridge in Paris that is in its original state is undoubtedly the Pont Neuf, a bridge in some form has existed at the site of the Pont Notre-Dame since antiquity; nonetheless, it has been destroyed and reconstructed numerous times, a fact referred to in the Latin inscription on it to honor its Italian architect, Fra Giovanni Giocondo. (See below.) The bridge once was lined with approximately sixty houses, the weight of which caused a collapse in 1499.

depictions.name: Pont Notre-Dame
depictions.text: The Pont Notre-Dame is a bridge that crosses the Seine in Paris, France connecting the northern part of the city with the Île de la Cité. Some form of the bridge existed at the same spot at the Seine since nearly the founding of Paris, although it was destroyed and replaced many times. In the early 1400s, the bridge consisted of a few wooden planks.
